# Zig 0.17 compatibility branch

This branch targets the released Zig **0.17.0** and preserves the authorship of
upstream [PR #3270](https://github.com/zigtools/zls/pull/3270), based on
`zigtools/zls` master `eab2be0fd74443a27662da809b771c4ad0d2afcf`.
The fork has a separate package fingerprint from the maintained upstream.

It uses Zig's actual build-server protocol and serialized module graph. It does
not infer import paths from source spelling or hard-code application modules.

## Additional fixes

- Grow the step map before inserting alternate top-level build steps. A real
  project with 32 alternate steps crashed the original draft; regression uses 48.
- Free the resolved build configuration when the build-server process fails
  after configuration extraction. A real process-exit wrapper reproduced arena
  leaks under `DebugAllocator` before the fix.
- Advance the build diagnostic version on successful configuration, including
  projects with no generated steps. Real `@compileError` diagnostics now clear
  after the build script is repaired.
- Populate build-script dependency imports from serialized package ownership.
  Both `b.dependency("pkg").module("pkg")` in application code and
  `@import("pkg")` in the build script are verified with a local dependency.

## Build and validate

Use Zig 0.17.0 on `PATH`:

```sh
zig build -Doptimize=safe
zig build test -Doptimize=safe
zig build test-build-system
```

`test-build-system` requires Python 3. It creates temporary projects and checks
real LSP hover responses for named modules, options, translated C, command
outputs, WriteFiles outputs, dependency build scripts, and diagnostic recovery.
It waits for asynchronous build configuration with a finite deadline; it does
not skip a failed semantic assertion. The debug build also reports allocator
leaks at shutdown.

The Zenit integration is independently verified with its 45-case real YIX/ZLS
smoke suite. From the Zenit root, use:

```sh
zig build dev-tools
zig build test-zls yix-lsp-smoke
```

The dependency is installed as `zig-out/bin/zenit-zls` (`zenit-zls.exe` on Windows).
Yix uses this executable automatically; other Zig editors can configure its absolute path.
See [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) for the pinned source revisions.

## Remaining protocol limitations

Zig 0.17's serialized configuration currently omits exported modules that are
not reachable from a compile step. A library that only calls `addModule`, with
no test/check/compile step, therefore still needs a normal check step exposing
that module to the graph, for example:

```zig
const target = b.standardTargetOptions(.{});
const lib = b.addModule("lib", .{
    .root_source_file = b.path("src/root.zig"),
    .target = target,
});
const check = b.addObject(.{ .name = "lib-check", .root_module = lib });
b.step("check", "Check the library").dependOn(&check.step);
```

Dependency build scripts are resolved when their package ownership is present
in a module or build step. Dependencies used solely by the build script and
absent from that serialized graph, and dependency aliases containing dots, are
not covered. Install-prefix-relative lazy paths also remain unsupported by the
upstream draft. These cases are not presented as fully supported.

The upstream work remains tracked in [#3208](https://github.com/zigtools/zls/issues/3208).
